message.content: {"items":[{"item_id":"h061","prompts":["I'm putting together a monthly security report and I have entries like {\"cve\": \"CVE-2021-44228\", \"nvd_score\": 10.0, \"ghsa_score\": null, \"redhat_score\": 9.8} and {\"cve\": \"CVE-2019-1234\", \"nvd_score\": null, \"ghsa_score\": 7.5, \"redhat_score\": 7.2}. Write me a small Python function that picks a single severity score per CVE with a sensible preference order across these sources, and make sure it doesn't crash when a vulnerability has no score anywhere."],"rubric":["Provides working code that reads the inline CVE score data","Implements an explicit priority order across NVD, GHSA, and RedHat sources","Handles missing/null scores gracefully, including CVEs with no score at all","Returns or prints one final score per CVE"]},{"item_id":"h062","prompts":["For the release automation summary I'm writing, look up the tag 'v1.4.2' in the GitHub repository 'vercel/next.js' and tell me its commit SHA, who created it, the date, and any message or release notes attached to it.","",""],"rubric":["Retrieves details for the tag v1.4.2 from vercel/next.js","Reports the tag's commit SHA and creation date","Includes tag message/annotation or notes if present","Does not fabricate details it could not retrieve"]},{"item_id":"h063","prompts":["Please pull the comments from the discussion about 'Roadmap for v2.0' in the GitHub repo 'obsidianmd/obsidian-help' and give me a summary of the main points people raised, listing each commenter and their key concern.","",""],"rubric":["Retrieves comments from the specified GitHub discussion","Lists distinct commenters along with their points","Provides an accurate summary rather than fabrication","Notes clearly if the discussion or comments could not be found"]},{"item_id":"h064","prompts":["I ran a small meet and want to rank the lifters fairly across weight classes. Results: Ben, 93kg class, squat 220kg, bench 150kg, deadlift 260kg; Tara, 63kg class, squat 145kg, bench 85kg, deadlift 170kg; Leo, 120kg class, squat 280kg, bench 190kg, deadlift 300kg. Calculate their totals and use a bodyweight-adjusted formula (like Wilks or DOTS) to tell me who actually performed best pound-for-pound.","",""],"rubric":["Computes correct three-lift totals for each lifter","Applies a recognized bodyweight-adjusted coefficient (e.g., Wilks/DOTS) with correct math","Ranks lifters by adjusted score, not raw total","Shows the intermediate values used"]},{"item_id":"h065","prompts":["Our HarmonyOS app works fine on phones but testers report the layout breaks on a foldable when it's half-open, and content gets hidden behind the camera area on a tablet. Walk me through how to approach fixing this: what adaptation areas I should check for screen/window size, fold state, and avoid areas, and give me a prioritized checklist for the foldable device issue.","",""],"rubric":["Identifies the relevant multi-device adaptation categories (screen/window size, fold state, avoid areas)","Addresses the foldable half-open scenario concretely","Provides a prioritized, actionable checklist","Does not stray into unrelated HarmonyOS topics"]},{"item_id":"h066","prompts":["I'm planning a trip and can't decide between flying and taking a taxi from Barcelona to Madrid. Estimate the driving distance and how long a taxi or drive would take, plus a rough fare, so I can compare it with a €60 flight.","",""],"rubric":["Provides an estimated driving distance between Barcelona and Madrid","Provides an estimated travel duration","Includes a rough cost estimate with stated assumptions","Presents the result in a way that supports comparison with the €60 flight"]},{"item_id":"h067","prompts":["I want to build an MCP server in Python that lets an AI assistant query our internal parts-inventory REST API (endpoints like GET /parts?sku=... and GET /parts/{id}/stock). Walk me through designing it well: project structure with FastMCP, tool definitions, input validation, error handling, and any best practices I should follow.","",""],"rubric":["Uses Python/FastMCP with a correct project structure","Defines tools for the sample inventory endpoints with typed parameters","Includes input validation and error handling guidance","Covers MCP-specific best practices (tool descriptions, resource vs tool, transport)"]},{"item_id":"h068","prompts":["Here are two quarters of 13-F holdings data for a fund: Q1 shows [{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"shares\": 100000, \"value\": 17500000}, {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"shares\": 50000, \"value\": 15000000}, {\"ticker\": \"TSLA\", \"shares\": 20000, \"value\": 4000000}]; Q2 shows [{\"ticker\": \"AAPL\", \"shares\": 120000, \"value\": 22800000}, {\"ticker\": \"MSFT\", \"shares\": 30000, \"value\": 10500000}, {\"ticker\": \"NVDA\", \"shares\": 15000, \"value\": 1800000}]. Analyze the quarter-over-quarter changes: total portfolio value, number of holdings, and which positions were added, trimmed, or exited.","",""],"rubric":["Correctly computes total portfolio value for each quarter","Reports change in number of holdings between quarters","Identifies new (NVDA), trimmed (MSFT), increased (AAPL) positions with correct numbers","Presents clear quarter-over-quarter insights"]},{"item_id":"h069","prompts":["I have a messy log file where each record starts with a timestamp line like '=== 2024-05-01 10:23:45 ===' followed by indented key: value lines such as '  status: OK' and '  user: alice'. Some values contain colons, and a few records are missing the 'status' key. Show me how to parse this into a list of dicts, handling the embedded colons and defaults for missing keys.","",""],"rubric":["Parses records delimited by the timestamp header lines","Handles values containing colons correctly","Applies a default for missing keys such as status","Produces a list of dictionaries with record data"]},{"item_id":"h070","prompts":["I found a SQLite file 'game_maps.db' with tables I don't recognize. Explain how I can inspect its schema, figure out how the tables relate to each other, and dump the map/tile data out as structured JSON. Use generic examples of what the tables might look like since you can't see my file.","",""],"rubric":["Explains how to inspect the SQLite schema (tables, columns, relations)","Covers identifying table relationships (foreign keys or inference)","Shows how to export the data as structured JSON","Uses concrete example queries/code rather than vague advice"]}]}
